title: Tempo-scan: sessionized latency & cost brief
body:
Objective:
Run a concentrated, reproducible sweep targeting mid-size conversational sessions (8 ± 2 turns) to surface practical latency vs cost tradeoffs for the console/SDK developer persona. This is a quick experimental brief — intended to guide a 2-week canary and dashboarding work.

Context and motivation:
- Many product teams use mid-length sessions (6–10 turns) for agent-style flows and assistants. These sessions expose interesting interactions between batching windows, KV cache prefetch, and quantization because workload is neither chat-lite nor long-document.
- We want a configuration that balance: low p99 latency (user-facing snappiness) and minimized $/1M tokens while limiting quality regressions.

Methodology (short):
- Workload: synthetic session generator seeded from 10 real customer session traces (anonymized). Target: 8 turns per session, mean tokens per session = 1.2k (SD ~250).
- Hardware: homogenous A100-like nodes (v2), single-model variant per run.
- Configs tested: SmallBatch (baseline), DynWindow (dynamic batching with 50ms window), Prefetch-KV (intent-aware KV prefetch +/- 200 tokens), Quant8 (INT8 model), Hybrid (Quant8 + Prefetch-KV).
- Measurements: p50/p90/p99 latency for full-response completion, tail-jank incidents (>=2x median), and normalized cost ($ per 1M tokens estimated from runtime GPU seconds * unit price). 20k sessions per config.
- Note: output quality checks limited to 50 eval prompts per config (automated ROUGE/embedding-sim test) — stated separately in action items.

Summary results (mid-size session cohort):

Config      | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | Cost ($/1M tokens)
------------|----------|----------|----------|------------------
SmallBatch  | 160      | 320      | 950      | 22.0
DynWindow   | 120      | 260      | 720      | 18.0
Prefetch-KV | 90       | 210      | 500      | 19.0
Quant8      | 100      | 230      | 600      | 14.0
Hybrid      | 75       | 180      | 420      | 12.0

Interpretation (quick):
- Hybrid (Quant8 + Prefetch-KV) dominates the tested space: lowest tail p99 and lowest cost. Quantization provides the cost win, prefetch reduces tail by avoiding cold KV misses.
- Prefetch-KV improves tail substantially over DynWindow at modest cost increase — useful when p99 matters more than per-token unit price.
- Dynamic batching helps P50 and P90 but leaves large p99 spikes: batching window amplifies microburst contention.

ASCII scatter (Cost on X, p99 on Y; lower-left = ideal):

Cost ($/1M) --> 10    12    14    16    18    20    22
p99(ms) |
 500  - |        Prefetch-KV
 600  - |              Quant8
 720  - |         DynWindow
 950  - | SmallBatch
 420  - | Hybrid  <-- best

Mini-breakdown (sampled telemetry):
- Hybrid utilization: steady GPU duty 68% (vs SmallBatch 52%) — better amortization of host transfers.
- Tail-jank incidents (>=2x median) per 10k sessions: SmallBatch 320, DynWindow 210, Prefetch-KV 90, Quant8 140, Hybrid 55.
- KV cache hit rate: Prefetch-KV 78%, Hybrid 81% (prefetch + quant overhead reduces cold misses).

Microcases observed:
- Long-initial-turn penalty: sessions with large first-turn (>400 tokens) cause DynamoWindow to delay many follow-ups — 15% of p99 incidents traced to initial-turn serialization. Prefetch avoids ~60% of those by warming KV slots.
- Multiplexing thrash: SmallBatch shows many short spikes when many small sessions co-locate; DynWindow smooths median but not the tail.

Quality check note (limited):
- Automated similarity vs FP32 baseline (50 eval prompts): Quant8 average embedding similarity = 0.982 (sd 0.007) — passes threshold for many features, but we flagged 6/50 prompts with degraded factuality signals. Action: run expanded eval for critical customers before broad rollouts.

Actionable recommendations (prioritized):
1) Canary Hybrid for mid-size session product teams (5% traffic) with automated rollback on sample-quality regressions. Add post-rollout gating based on p99 and embedding-sim thresholds.
2) Expose "prefetch aggressiveness" knob in console: default medium for assistant workloads; per-route override.
3) Add a sessionized p99 metric to the latency dashboard (session boundary-aware) and instrument KV-prefetch hit rate as a first-class cost-saving signal.
4) Run a focused quantization QA: 3k eval prompts across safety/QA/long-turn prompts to validate the 6/50 failure mode.
5) For teams that cannot accept any quality drift, recommend Prefetch-KV (no quant) as the p99-friendly option; cost still ~13% better than baseline in practice due to reduced tail.

Implementation notes and risks:
- Risk: customer workloads with unpredictable, long initial turns may still see p99 degradation; consider initial-turn fast-path or adapt prefetch thresholds.
- Operational: Hybrid requires both quantized model packaging and the prefetch coordination hook; coordinate runtime PR and model onboarding (linked PR above).

Next steps (two-week cadence):
- Week 1: prepare canary build (runtime + quant produce), expand eval set, UX knob prototype in console (Marcus).
- Week 2: 5% canary, collect 100k session telemetry, run automated quality signal checks, decide roll-to-100% or rollback.

Appendix: short run parameters
- Sessions per run: 20,000
- Seed traces: 10 anonymized customer conversation templates
- Token distribution: mean 1.2k / session (turns=8±2)
- Pricing assumption: unit GPU second = $0.45, transformation to $/1M tokens uses observed token/sec per config

Notes to self: capture raw trace sample for the 6 flagged prompts (Aisha) and create a dedicated eval ticket (JIRA-OPT-4567).
